project_tracker_diagnostic: Annual; lower leaves opposite and upper leaves alternate; blades 1–2-pinnately lobed; male heads form terminal spikes and female heads sit below in leaf axils.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common, conspicuous, or high-value comparison species for Central Texas field ID.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual from seed; does not produce a persistent network of perennial underground rhizomes. An established western ragweed patch may have multiple stems connected belowground.
morphology_keys.habit: Erect, branching herb of disturbed ground.
morphology_keys.leaves: Lower leaves opposite, upper leaves alternate; blades generally deeply once- or twice-divided into narrow lobes. Examine leaf position along the same stem rather than one isolated leaf.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small drooping male pollen-bearing heads arranged along terminal spikes, with tiny separate female heads below in the upper leaf axils. Both sexes occur on the same plant.
morphology_keys.fruit: Female heads mature into small woody burrlike involucres with usually 4–7 short spines or projections; photograph mature fruit beside a ruler.
best_field_traits: Annual plant with opposite lower leaves, alternate upper leaves
Dangling male heads in terminal spikes; small female heads beneath
Small woody fruit with short crownlike projections

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

look_here_first: START WITH THE LEAVES: common ragweed is an ANNUAL with finely divided, fernlike leaves, usually opposite low on the stem and alternate above. NEXT inspect flowering stems: dangling greenish MALE pollen heads form terminal spikes; much smaller FEMALE heads sit below them near the upper leaf axils. FINALLY check the mature fruit: a small woody bur with several short pointed projections. Western ragweed can have similar flowers and divided leaves but is a perennial spreading from underground rhizomes; check connected stems if uncertain.

key_distinctions.look_here_first: Follow multiple stems below ground and compare leaf lobes.
key_distinctions.common_ragweed: Annual without persistent connecting rhizomes; leaves frequently finely divided.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Western ragweed is rhizomatous perennial with broader and often less finely cut lobes.
key_distinctions.caution: Leaves overlap, and mowing changes habit. Rhizome connection is strongest when available.

key_distinctions.common_ragweed: Leaves are finely pinnately divided into many narrow segments.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Giant ragweed has very large leaves usually with 3 (sometimes 5) broad palmate lobes.
key_distinctions.caution: Young plants may have variable leaves; compare multiple mature leaves.

key_distinctions.look_here_first: Inspect reproductive heads and leaf odor only as supporting evidence.
key_distinctions.common_ragweed: Separate dangling male heads in terminal spikes, tiny female heads lower, crownlike burs.
key_distinctions.lookalike: Sageworts have different composite flower heads and often aromatic or silvery foliage; inspect flowers to confirm.
key_distinctions.caution: Aromatic foliage is not a reliable standalone test.
